examiner_notes.quote: This was another question where many candidates had no idea of how or where to begin. There were many blank responses as well as an equal number that scored no marks at all.
Those that did manage to score marks tended to score most of them.
It is worth repeating that it is good practice in a geometric question to sketch out a diagram.

In part (a) most incorrect responses attempted to set 4 4 4 2 3 . 3 0 3 5 5 − −         − − =         − +     λ λ λ rather than 4 . 3 0 5 AX −     − =        This immediately resulted in 0 marks for (a)(i).
examiner_notes.display: In part (a) most incorrect responses attempted to set $\begin{pmatrix}4-4\lambda\\2-3\lambda\\-3+5\lambda\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}-4\\-3\\5\end{pmatrix}=0$ rather than $\overrightarrow{AX}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}-4\\-3\\5\end{pmatrix}=0$ This immediately resulted in 0 marks for (a)(i).

examiner_notes.quote: Most candidates who attempted the latter scored 4 or 5 marks.
Candidates who got an incorrect X could still pick up method marks in (a)(ii) and (b) but many gave up after part (a).
Other methods were seen in part (a) including minimising the length of AX using either differentiation or by completing the square.
